item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Done:

http://scp-nala.wikidot.com/statistics:rating-by-day

  • Articles posted on Friday have an average rating a full ten points higher than those posted on Sunday, Monday, or Tuesday, almost a full 16% increase.
  • Articles posted on Friday are eight points higher than those posted on Saturday, and five points higher than those posted Wednesday or Thursday.
  • 10% to 40% more articles are posted on Friday than any other day of the week.

I included a by-month chart just for kicks and giggles:

  • Submission count increases in May (when students get out of school) and July (when people get back from vacation or are otherwise bored) and drop sharply in September (when students go back to school).
  • Submission quality drops slightly in May and increases slightly in September.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
That can be done for the final tally easily enough, but it doesn't change the fact that even contributors may not necessarily be around for a while.

Take a simple example:

A contributor is around for the first two weeks of the contest, reads and votes on two or three articles. They then go on a vacation for two weeks, missing the latter half of the contest and thus not voting on anything else past the point they left, even if they liked some of those more than the ones that came before.

Edit: Wow, I didn't even realize that today was the first day of school in most parts. That by itself is a huge deal, as proven year over year by site statistics.
There's just a lot of variables that aren't being accounted for, and while they may not necessarily be a big deal, it's worrisome from a data collection point of view.

It helps, but it doesn't eliminate the 'snapshot vote effect'; kids who tend to join the site for no longer than a week before getting bored. In that time, they may drop some votes on the most recently written articles and not stick around to read much less vote on anything else.

Though the only way to fix this is limit voting to contributors only… which currently isn't possible… that I know of. (I am not a techie)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
but in the future perhaps we should consider having all submissions put up at once?

It's true that earlier submissions have the benefit of having a longer period to vote, but later submissions have the benefit of more time to edit and time to get reviewed.

It would be more fair to put them all up at the same time, but I think it might be less fun for the readers (and the writers as well). It also might make it a bit more complicated, administration wise, for the contest starter.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I had thought of that. Most of the rating an article gets is on account of exposure, so early submissions do get kind of an edge.

However, over the course of the contest? I don't know that it's enough to make a big difference. The most dense voting activity of an article is within the first two to three weeks. For two articles of comparable quality/popularity, you could probably only expect a difference of 2-6 votes between one submitted August 1st and one submitted on August 31.

So yeah, it could make a difference, but so far the ratings are separated by a much wider margin. They were in the last contest as well. And though it has clearly been much longer, it looks like the other ones were, too.

Maybe if two ratings are really close the judges could state a policy to make a decision based on their thoughts about the piece's artistic merit and how well it answered the prompt. But it doesn't look like that will be necessary any time in the near future. Just my two cents.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
You know, I was just thinking today that there's a unique problem to using raw rating as the basis for final scoring in these contests, namely that not all submissions are posted at the same time and that the nature of voters on the SCP wiki is that they may not necessarily read or even see all submissions. It's a bit late to change for this contest, but in the future perhaps we should consider having all submissions put up at once?

Not that I'm complaining with regards to my own entry, I have no illusions about that one winning. :)
